messages.subject: multiple models
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm new to the Bayesian approach and RStan so I apologize in advance if this is a simple question or has been answered elsewhere.

I'd like to check the way RStan is reading and parsing my data for a hierarchical model so I would like to create multiple simple linear models within one RStan script (if possible) that would be similar to a random slope and intercept model (see below; a partial pooling model).

I would like to build this model for each of my 71 species (i.e. 71 models) within RStan rather than building a loop in R and running RStan 71 times:

data {

  int<lower=0> N;

  vector [N] y; // day of year 

  vector [N] year; //x vector

  }

parameters {

  real alpha; //intercept

  real beta; //slope

  real<lower=0> sigma; //regression variance

}

model {

y~normal(alpha+beta*year, sigma);

  }


My hierarchical model looks like this:


data {

  int N;                                // # data points

  int J;                                // # species

  vector[N] y;                          // day of year

  int species[N];                       // species identity, 

  vector[N] year;                       // year of data point

  int nVars; //number of predictors

  matrix[nVars, nVars] Imat;

}

parameters {

  vector[J] alpha;                          // the intercept for each species

  vector[J] beta;                          // the slope for each species

  real<lower=0> sigma_y;                // measurement error

  cov_matrix[nVars] Omega3;

 

  // hyperparameters

  real mu_a;                            // mean intercept across species

  real<lower=0> sigma_a;                // variation of intercept among species; 

  real mu_b;                            // mean slope across species

  real<lower=0> sigma_b;                // variation of slope among species; 

}


model {

real ypred[N];

 Omega3 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);  //priors for covariance matrix

 

  for (i in 1:N){

    ypred[i] <- alpha[species[i]] + beta[species[i]] * year[i];

  }

  y ~ normal(ypred, sigma_y);

  alpha ~ normal(mu_a, sigma_a);

  beta ~ normal(mu_b, sigma_b);

}


Is this possible?.


I am using RStan version 2.6 in R version 3.1.3.


Thanks in advance,

Heather

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multiple models
parts:
Yes, you can fit multiple models at once. You just have to make
sure they don't share parameters. All you need to do is add another
layer of indexing to the data and parameters.

For example, if you wanted to do something simple:

data {
int N;
real y[N];
}
parameters {
real mu;
}
model {
y ~ normal(mu, 1);
}

and you have M data sets, you want to do this:

data {
int M;
int N[M];
real y[M,N];
}
parameters {
real mu[M];
}
model {
for (m in 1:M)
y[m] ~ normal(mu[m], 1);
}

It may actually be faster to fit a single model 71 times than to
fit a big model once.

- Bob

You're right --- you need to declare any variable that's used
in Stan.

The vector type only takes one arg and produces a column vector:

vector[M] u;

The matrix type takes two args and produces a dense matrix:

matrix[M,N] v;

There's also arrays:

real v[M,N];

There's a chapter near the front of the manual about the differences.

- Bob

parts:
The problem is that the matrix declaration you have:

> matrix[M,N] y;

isn't compatible with the declaration of N:

> int N[M];


The matrix declaration needs an integer, but you've
given it an array of integers.

- Bob
